title: Pathfinder 1:1 brief — Cassidy Park
content:
Context:
- Weekly 1:1 with report (Ava Li). Role: Senior SW Eng on inference-serving. Goal of this session: unblock near-term rollout decisions, quick career coaching, and align on experiment vs canary for v0.9.

Meeting logistics:
- Target duration: 30 minutes (can extend to 45 if needed).
- Location: Zoom -> link from calendar.
- Prep request to Ava: bring a one-slide summary of canary telemetry (p50/p95, errors, cost delta).

Agenda (30m):
1) Quick personal check-in (5m)
   - How was weekend? energy level. Anything blocking focus? (mental load, meetings)
2) Signals from the sprint (7m)
   - Recent telemetry: p95 latency moved from ~32ms -> ~38ms after the KV-cache proto change (unexpected).
   - Error spike on txn-id mapping during high batch windows (SERV-4123).
   - Cost note: token-cost per 1000 down ~12% in perf env due to batching tweak.
3) v0.9 canary decision (10m)
   - Options: roll canary now with reduced traffic + global fallback vs delay until fixes for txn mapping.
   - Key risk: customer-facing errors if fallback not healthy.
   - My leaning: canary with strict traffic cap (5%) and immediate rollback trigger on any symptomatic errors.
4) Career / growth (5m)
   - Ava prep: pick one recent PR that shows cross-team impact.
   - Discuss next stretch: own the canary playbook + run a postmortem runbook.
5) Quick action item review & close (3m)

Notes to self (manager):
- Keep tone low-friction; the latency increase may be demoralizing — focus on hypothesis-driven debugging.
- Encourage Ava to own the rollout checklist; it's a good visibility opportunity.
- If Ava asks for extra headcount: default to contractor trial (4–6 weeks) and measure throughput uplift.

Preparation checklist (for me before meeting):
- Pull canary telemetry snapshot (last 48h) and highlight anomalies.
- Read SERV-4123 thread and mark two concrete technical questions for Ava.
- Jot a one-paragraph rubric for canary rollback thresholds (errors/sec > X, p95 > baseline + 15%, customer-500 rate).

Hypotheses for latency regression:
- New KV-cache eviction behavior causing more cache misses for long-tail keys. Verify cache hit rate by key-size bucket.
- Kernel selection fallback on certain instance types after driver update — check node-level logs.
- Batch size distribution shifted higher due to client-side SDK change; confirm via tracing.

Decision criteria for canary (proposed):
- Start traffic at 5% global, keep for 3 hours.
- Auto-cut if:
  - customer-error rate increases > 0.5% absolute OR
  - p95 > baseline + 15% for two consecutive 10-min windows OR
  - any new 5xx errors tied to txn mapping.
- If cut, immediate rollback to previous variant + postmortem to be owned by Ava within 48h.

Action items (to track after meeting):
- Ava: produce a one-slide canary telemetry summary + explicit rollback triggers (due: 2027-04-14).
- Cassidy (me): draft rollout config for ops (traffic caps, monitoring alerts) and share with SRE (due: 2027-04-13).
- Mateo: quick audit of node driver changes and confirm none applied to canary pool (due: 2027-04-13).
- Rina: validate KV-cache metric dashboards include hit-rate by key-length bucket (due: 2027-04-15).

Coaching prompts (to ask Ava):
- Walk me through the top-three hypotheses you would triage and what evidence would convince you to rollback.
- How would you explain the risk tradeoffs for proceeding with a small canary to a PM who is pushing to ship?
- What's one thing you want to learn from this canary that will level up your system-design sense?

Open questions for follow-up:
- Is the txn-id mapping error reproducible with a small synthetic load? (who will own repro?)
- Do we have alerting gaps for 4xx->5xx transitions in the new batching path?

Wrap-up script (closing the 1:1):
- "Thanks — this landed a clear plan. I'll own the rollout config and follow up with SRE; you'll own the telemetry slide and postmortem if needed. Let's sync briefly tomorrow if anything turns red."

Post-meeting capture (to update after):
- Meeting outcome: (fill after)
- Decisions made: (fill after)
- New action items / owners: (fill after)

Quick personal reminder (notes to self):
- Give Ava autonomy on playbook edits; provide guardrails not micromanagement.
- Recognize the visibility if canary goes well — call out in team channel and flag for Eng All-hands.
summary: 30m 1:1 prep for canary decision + career checkpoint. Focus: latency regression, rollout plan, and concrete action items.
